Visitor guide · Humahuaca, Jujuy

Plaza Sargento Mariano Gómez (Humahuaca)

Welcome to Plaza Sargento Mariano Gómez, also known as the central plaza of Humahuaca or Plaza Humahuaca. This public square stands at the heart of Humahuaca, Jujuy, within the Quebrada de Humahuaca of Argentina.

Your starting point

About Plaza Sargento Mariano Gómez and its geographic context.

Jujuy’s tourism manual places the square opposite the Cabildo. It describes the mechanical San Francisco Solano figure at noon, but does not confirm operation today: check locally before planning around it. The Heroes of Independence Monument is reached by stairs; plan that separate visit around your access needs.

Plaza Sargento Mariano Gómez sits in the historic centre of Humahuaca, in northern Jujuy Province, within the Andean cultural corridor recognised by UNESCO.

UNESCO describes the gorge as a communication and trade route with evidence spanning more than 10,000 years, where landscape, architecture and community practices remain connected. In that setting, Plaza Sargento Mariano Gómez serves as a civic core and orientation point for moving through Humahuaca’s urban fabric.

Practical reading

Location and how to get to the square in Humahuaca.

This guide gathers practical references to locate Plaza Sargento Mariano Gómez, understand its position within the historic centre, and plan a sensible arrival without replacing local notices or safety information.

01

Access and cost

The plaza is public space. No specific entry charge is indicated; nearby museums, excursions, events and services may set their own conditions.

02

Best time to visit

Morning and early afternoon generally suit an unhurried walk. The setting is dry and high-altitude: prioritise shade, water and sun protection, and bring an extra layer for temperature changes.

03

Suggested time

Allow time to walk the immediate area and orient your visit. If you plan to add churches, viewpoints, trails, museums or neighbouring villages, allow a broader, flexible day.

04

Check locally

Google Maps, checked 23 October 2026: 4.6/5 from 5,171 reviews and a 24-hour listing for the square. This third-party listing does not guarantee unrestricted access or opening hours for the Cabildo, church, museums or shops.

Arrive with care

How to reach Plaza Sargento Mariano Gómez.

A

From the airport

Regional air access is through the San Salvador de Jujuy area. From there, the journey to Humahuaca continues by road. Leave a comfortable margin, especially when connecting flights and ground transport.

B

Intercity bus

Long- and medium-distance services connect the gorge with other parts of Jujuy. Check timetables, stops, luggage policies and service changes directly with operators or a local information point before travelling.

C

Taxi, remís or transfer

For groups, luggage or unscheduled itineraries, ask about authorised taxi, remís or transfer services. Agree on the route, fare and meeting point before the journey begins.

D

Private vehicle

National Route 9 structures access to the town. Check road conditions, fuel, weather and signage before driving in highland areas. Park only where permitted and keep pedestrian access clear.

Around the plaza

Landmarks around Plaza Sargento Mariano Gómez.

Use the square to orient yourself between separate buildings and spaces: the Cabildo de Humahuaca with the clock and mechanical image of San Francisco Solano, the Iglesia Catedral de Nuestra Señora de la Candelaria, and the Monumento a los Héroes de la Independencia.

01 · Cabildo

Cabildo de Humahuaca

Facing the square stands the Cabildo de Humahuaca, a civic building associated with the clock and mechanical image of San Francisco Solano. Its presence helps place the historic centre precisely around Plaza Sargento Mariano Gómez.

02 · Cathedral

Nuestra Señora de la Candelaria

The Iglesia Catedral de Nuestra Señora de la Candelaria forms part of the same immediate urban ensemble. The church is a separate visit: check its opening, access and religious activities before entering.

03 · Monument

Heroes of Independence

On the nearby hillside rises the Monumento a los Héroes de la Independencia, one of the visual landmarks most closely tied to Humahuaca. The square works as a pedestrian forecourt and starting point for reading that historic landscape.

04 · Centre

Historic centre of Humahuaca

The square also organises the reading of the urban layout: streets, public buildings, church space, and visitor circulation converge here. That is why Plaza Humahuaca and Plaza Sargento Mariano Gómez often refer to the same central urban core.

Plan your route

What to see and do in Humahuaca

The square is the natural starting point for exploring Humahuaca and the Quebrada de Humahuaca. Heritage landmarks, local handicrafts and places to stay come together here as you explore the region.

01 · What to see

Landmarks around the square

Facing the square stand the Cabildo de Humahuaca and the Iglesia Catedral de Nuestra Señora de la Candelaria; on the nearby hillside rises the Monumento a los Héroes de la Independencia. Together they form the historic core you can walk.

02 · Handicrafts

Handicrafts and market in Humahuaca

If you find stalls or a market, ask about makers, materials and prices. Vendors and their hours can vary; this guide does not publish a trading calendar.

03 · Stay

Camping and lodging in Humahuaca

Staying overnight or camping requires separate planning. This guide does not confirm permission to camp in the square or campsite availability. Check authorized accommodation, season and services before booking.

History and memory

Mariano Gómez, Humahuaca, and the civic memory of the square.

The name Plaza Sargento Mariano Gómez links this public space with Humahuaca’s historic memory and with the independence-era episodes of northern Argentina. More than an isolated square, it acts as a civic stage where urban history, local religious life, and the reading of the quebrada landscape converge.

To extend the visit, consider nearby public and heritage landmarks such as the Monumento a los Héroes de la Independencia, the Cabildo, the cathedral, the town museums, the Coctaca terraces, or views towards Hornocal. Verify access, conditions, and local guidance for each outing.

Frequently asked questions

One final practical read before you travel.

Does the plaza have visiting hours?

The Google Maps listing checked 23 October 2026 shows 24 hours for the square. This is not the opening schedule of the church, Cabildo or museums; check access on the day.

Is there parking by the plaza?

Street parking may be available, subject to signs, availability and local controls. Do not assume that a reserved area exists.

What should I consider about altitude?

Adjust your pace, drink water, use sun protection and carry layers for temperature changes. If you have health-related questions, consult a professional before travelling.

Is there an admission fee?

No specific entry charge is indicated for the plaza. Other nearby services, activities or venues may have their own conditions.

Which street is the square on?

Plaza Sargento Mariano Gómez sits in the historic centre of Humahuaca, Jujuy, facing the Cabildo and the cathedral. Its approximate coordinates are −23.2039735, −65.3487032.

Is there camping in Humahuaca?

This guide does not confirm permission to camp in the square or campsite availability. Plan accommodation separately and check authorized services and local rules.
